PRD: Orion Studio v3.0
Owner: Marcos Rivera | Status: In Review | Last updated: June 18, 2026

1. Overview

Studio v3.0 is a major release focused on enterprise readiness. Following the March reorg and feedback from enterprise prospects (especially Meridian Corp), we're shifting priorities from collaboration features to security, compliance, and authentication infrastructure.

This is a strategic pivot from the original v3.0 plan. The pre-reorg roadmap had collaboration features (real-time editing, inline comments, team workspaces) as the headline. Those are now pushed to v3.1. I want to be transparent: this is the right call for the business, but it means we're deprioritizing the features that made Studio loved by individual developers. We need to be careful not to lose our core audience while chasing enterprise.

2. Timeline

Internal beta: July 28, 2026
GA launch: August 15, 2026
Full rollout (all customers migrated): August 22, 2026

These dates are tight. Jake estimates 2 weeks of buffer have been consumed by the auth overhaul scope expansion. If the API auth consolidation (see section 4.1) slips, we slip.

3. Goals & Success Metrics

G1: Unblock 3+ enterprise deals currently stalled on security features
  - KR: Meridian procurement team signs off on security review by August 30
  - KR: Zero critical security findings in third-party pen test

G2: Maintain developer satisfaction through the transition
  - KR: NPS stays above 45 (currently 52)
  - KR: <5% increase in churn among individual/team plans

G3: Establish foundation for SOC2 Type II audit
  - KR: Audit logging implemented for all user-facing actions
  - KR: Role-based access control shipped with at least 3 predefined roles

4. Feature Scope

4.1 API Authentication Overhaul (P0 — blocks Meridian)
Current state: 3-step token exchange (app token → user token → scoped token). Enterprise customers hate this.
Target state: Single OAuth2 + PKCE flow. Support for SAML/SSO via Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace.
API key rotation without downtime (Meridian requires 90-day rotation policy).
Owner: Jake Kim | Eng estimate: 6 weeks | Status: In progress, 40% complete

4.2 Audit Logging (P0 — SOC2 requirement)
Log all user actions: login, API calls, permission changes, data exports.
Retention: 12 months minimum (Meridian wants 24 months).
Export format: JSON lines, S3-compatible.
Owner: Jake Kim | Eng estimate: 3 weeks | Status: Not started

4.3 Role-Based Access Control (P1)
Three default roles: Admin, Developer, Viewer.
Custom roles in v3.1.
Permission matrix: TBD — need input from Sarah on the UI.
Owner: Marcos Rivera | Eng estimate: 2 weeks | Status: Design phase

4.4 Collaboration Features (DESCOPED to v3.1)
Real-time co-editing, inline comments, team workspaces.
Pushed to v3.1 (target: October 2026).
Reason: Enterprise features take priority. Anya's call, Marcos agrees reluctantly.
Original designs still valid — see Figma link: [LINK REMOVED — ask Sarah]

5. Dependencies

- gRPC migration must reach 80% endpoint coverage before auth overhaul can ship (currently at 60%). Jake says this is the single biggest risk.
- Dashboard component library cleanup — Sarah flagged 3 different date pickers and 2 modal systems. Not a blocker for v3.0 but it's slowing the RBAC UI work.
- SOC2 readiness depends on audit logging shipping first. No audit logging = no SOC2 timeline.

6. Risks

- Auth overhaul is on the critical path. If it slips 2+ weeks, GA moves to September.
- We're running hot — Jake's team has no slack in the sprint. Any surprise (outage, critical bug) could cascade.
- Developer NPS risk: we're shipping zero developer-facing features in this release. Need strong messaging about what's coming in v3.1.

7. Open Questions

- Do we need a public changelog or migration guide for the auth changes? (Marcos thinks yes, Jake thinks it's premature)
- Should Enterprise tier customers get early access to v3.0 features before GA? Tom is pushing for this.
- What's the rollback plan if the auth migration breaks existing integrations? Jake: 'We'll have a feature flag, but rolling back OAuth changes is never clean.'

---
Document history:
- v1 (Feb 12): Original v3.0 plan with collaboration features
- v2 (Mar 28): Post-reorg rewrite — enterprise focus
- v3 (Jun 18): Current — scope locked, timeline confirmed

PRD: Orion Connect — API Marketplace & Gateway
Owner: Priya Sharma | Status: Living Document | Last updated: June 10, 2026

1. Product Overview

Orion Connect is our API marketplace and gateway product, launched December 2025. It enables engineering teams to discover, publish, and consume internal and third-party APIs through a unified platform. Think of it as an app store for APIs, combined with an API gateway that handles auth, rate limiting, and monitoring.

Connect was created to expand Orion's TAM beyond the IDE/developer tool space. Studio gives us the 'build' workflow; Connect gives us the 'integrate' workflow. Together they form a full developer experience platform.

As of June 2026, Connect has 31 published integrations (12 first-party, 19 partner-built) and 38 active enterprise accounts.

2. Target Users

Primary: Platform engineering teams (50-500 engineers) managing internal API ecosystems.
Secondary: Developer advocates and partner teams publishing public APIs.
Tertiary: Individual developers discovering and testing APIs.

3. Key Features (Current)

3.1 API Marketplace
- Browse and search published APIs with documentation
- Interactive API playground (try-before-you-integrate)
- SDK generation (TypeScript, Python, Go)
- Publisher dashboard with analytics

3.2 API Gateway
- Request routing and load balancing
- Rate limiting (configurable per consumer, per plan)
- Authentication proxy (currently basic API key, OAuth2 coming in Studio v3.0 integration)
- Real-time monitoring and alerting

3.3 Integration Management
- Dependency mapping (which services depend on which APIs)
- Version management and deprecation workflows
- Health checks and uptime monitoring

4. Pricing

See pricing sheet for full breakdown. Summary:
- Free: 100 API calls/day, up to 5 integrations. Good for evaluation and small teams.
- Pro ($299/month): 10,000 calls/day, 25 integrations, priority support, basic analytics.
- Enterprise (custom, starts at ~$1,200/month): Unlimited calls, SSO, audit logs, dedicated CSM, SLA guarantees, custom rate limits.

Note: Tom wants us to reconsider Enterprise pricing — he thinks $1,200 starting point is too high relative to Postman's team plan. We haven't made a decision yet. Need more data on competitive pricing.

5. Q3 Priorities

- Grow to 50 published integrations (target: 30 partner + 20 first-party)
- Reduce API gateway p99 latency from 340ms to <200ms (current bottleneck: auth proxy)
- Close 3 enterprise deals (Meridian, Arclight, Vossen)
- Ship Connect + Studio SSO integration (depends on Studio v3.0 auth overhaul)

6. Competitive Landscape

Direct: Postman (API platform), Kong (API gateway), RapidAPI (marketplace)
Indirect: AWS API Gateway, Apigee, MuleSoft

Our edge: We're the only platform that combines IDE (Studio) + marketplace (Connect) natively. Developers don't leave the Orion ecosystem.

7. Open Items

- Partner program terms need legal review (in progress)
- Billing integration with Stripe — currently manual for Enterprise tier
- Connect mobile experience: not planned. Mobile was killed (separate decision — see decision log).

content:
Decision Log: Cancellation of Orion Mobile
Date: June 2, 2026 | Decision maker: Anya Patel (CPO)
Stakeholders consulted: Marcos Rivera, Jake Kim, Tom Walsh

Decision: Cancel the Orion Mobile project effective immediately. Reallocate engineering resources (2.5 FTEs) to the Orion Connect team.

Context:
We launched an 8-week mobile pilot on April 1 to validate whether a native companion app would drive engagement and reduce churn. The hypothesis was that mobile access would increase daily touchpoints with Orion, especially for on-call developers.

Results:
The pilot did not meet any of its success thresholds:

| Metric | Target | Actual |
|--------|--------|--------|
| DAU | 500 | 120 |
| Avg session length | 5 min | 2.3 min |
| NPS | 40+ | 31 |
| % of total sessions | 10% | 2.8% |

Rationale for cancellation:
1. Low adoption: 120 DAU represents ~8% of our active user base. Even optimistically, mobile would cap at 5% of total platform usage.
2. High cost: 2.5 FTEs maintaining a native app (iOS + Android) for <3% of sessions is not justifiable at our stage.
3. Opportunity cost: Those 2.5 FTEs are desperately needed on Connect, which has a direct revenue path (enterprise deals) that mobile does not.
4. User feedback signal: Most pilot users said they prefer Slack notifications over a dedicated app. Our users are already at their desks — mobile access is a 'nice to have', not a workflow need.

Alternatives considered:
- PWA instead of native: Cheaper but same adoption problem. Rejected.
- Mobile-responsive web: Already works. Low investment, low reward. Will maintain but not invest.
- Revisit in 12 months: Open to it if user base grows 3x+ and we hear mobile demand in sales calls.

This decision was unanimous. Marcos initially advocated for the PWA approach but agreed after reviewing the session length data — even users who opened the app weren't doing meaningful work.

- Marcos: Archive mobile PRD and backlog
- Jake: Reassign mobile engineers to Connect by June 9
- Tom: Remove mobile from sales deck and website
- Anya: Communicate to team at next all-hands (June 5)

User Research: Meridian Corp — Enterprise Evaluation Feedback
Researcher: Priya Sharma | Date: May 14-16, 2026
Participants: Dana Torres (VP Engineering), Raj Kapoor (Platform Lead), Mei Lin (Senior Developer)

Background:
Meridian Corp (Fortune 500, financial services) is evaluating Orion for their platform engineering team (~200 developers). They're our largest enterprise prospect — deal value $180K/year. They completed a 30-day technical evaluation in May. This document summarizes their feedback.

---

Finding 1: API Authentication Flow is Too Complex (CRITICAL)

All three participants independently flagged this as the #1 blocker.

Current Orion auth requires 3 separate token exchanges:
1. App-level token (service credentials)
2. User-level token (developer identity)
3. Scoped token (per-API permissions)

Dana: 'Our developers are used to a single OAuth2 flow. Three token exchanges is a non-starter for adoption. We'd spend more time onboarding people to your auth system than the actual tool.'

Raj: 'I tried to write a wrapper library to abstract the 3 steps into 1 call. It took me 2 days and it's fragile. If your auth changes, my wrapper breaks.'

Mei: 'I gave up after the second token exchange and just used curl with hardcoded tokens. Which I know is terrible, but the flow was too frustrating.'

Impact: This is a procurement blocker. Meridian's security team will not approve a tool that requires developers to manage 3 separate tokens. They want single OAuth2 or SAML.

---

Finding 2: No Audit Logging for Compliance (HIGH)

Meridian is in financial services — SOX and SOC2 compliance are non-negotiable.

Dana: 'We need a complete audit trail of who did what, when. API calls, permission changes, data access — everything. Right now Orion is a black box from a compliance perspective.'

Raj: 'Our compliance team asked me for Orion's audit log API. I had to tell them it doesn't exist. That was an uncomfortable conversation.'

Impact: Without audit logging, Meridian's compliance team cannot approve Orion for production use. This is a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have.

---

Finding 3: Rate Limiting Too Aggressive for Enterprise Workloads (MEDIUM)

Meridian's platform team runs batch jobs that make thousands of API calls in short bursts.

Raj: 'We hit the rate limit within 10 minutes of our first integration test. The default limits assume interactive usage, not CI/CD pipelines.'

Current default: 100 requests/minute on Pro plan.
Meridian needs: 5,000+ requests/minute for their deployment pipeline.

Enterprise tier has custom limits but the configuration UX is poor — Raj said it took 45 minutes to figure out how to set custom rate limits.

---

Finding 4: Onboarding Took Too Long (MEDIUM)

Meridian's target: 1 week from signup to first production integration.
Actual time: 3 weeks.

Breakdown of delays:
- Week 1: Auth setup and troubleshooting (see Finding 1)
- Week 2: SDK generation issues (Python SDK had stale docs)
- Week 3: Rate limiting configuration + first successful integration test

Mei: 'The product itself is good once you get past the setup. But 3 weeks is too long. We tried Postman's API platform and were up in 2 days.'

---

Overall Sentiment:
- Product quality: 7/10 — 'the core is solid, especially the marketplace discovery experience'
- Onboarding: 3/10 — 'painful, would not recommend to a colleague'
- Enterprise readiness: 4/10 — 'not there yet, but the roadmap looks promising'

Dana's closing comment: 'We want this to work. Orion is the best product in this space for our use case. But my procurement team won't sign off until auth is simplified and we have audit logs. Get those done and we'll close in 30 days.'

---

Recommendations:
1. API auth simplification is THE priority. Nothing else matters until this ships.
2. Audit logging should be in v3.0 scope (confirmed — it is).
3. Enterprise onboarding playbook needed — not just docs, but a guided setup experience.
4. Rate limit defaults for Enterprise tier need to be 10x higher than current.

Technical Architecture: Orion API Gateway & Auth System
Author: Jake Kim (Engineering Lead) | Last updated: June 15, 2026
Status: Living document — reflects current + planned architecture

1. Infrastructure Overview

Orion runs on AWS. Key services:
- Compute: ECS Fargate (API services), Lambda (async jobs, webhooks)
- Database: PostgreSQL 15 on RDS (primary data), Redis 7 on ElastiCache (caching, sessions)
- Storage: S3 (assets, exports, backups)
- CDN: CloudFront (static assets, SDK distribution)
- Monitoring: Datadog (metrics, traces), PagerDuty (alerting)
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions → ECR → ECS deployment

We're considering TimescaleDB for usage analytics — currently analytics queries run on the main PostgreSQL instance which is causing slow reads during peak hours. No decision yet.

2. API Architecture — Current State

We're mid-migration from REST to gRPC for internal service communication.

Current: 60% of endpoints migrated to gRPC. 40% still on REST.
- gRPC: service-to-service calls (Studio backend → Connect gateway, auth service → user service)
- REST: all public-facing APIs, webhook delivery, third-party integrations

This dual stack creates maintenance overhead. Every new endpoint needs both REST and gRPC implementations until migration is complete. Estimated 3 sprints to finish.

The REST endpoints follow OpenAPI 3.0 spec. gRPC uses Protocol Buffers v3. We auto-generate REST docs from OpenAPI but gRPC docs are manual — this is a known gap.

3. Authentication Architecture

3.1 Current Auth Flow (Legacy — being replaced in v3.0)

Three-step token exchange:
1. Client sends service credentials → receives app token (valid 24h)
2. Client sends app token + user credentials → receives user token (valid 1h)
3. Client sends user token + requested scopes → receives scoped token (valid 1h)

This was designed for security granularity but in practice it's too complex. Meridian's feedback confirmed what we suspected: enterprises won't adopt a 3-step auth flow.

3.2 Target Auth Flow (v3.0 — shipping August 2026)

Single OAuth2 + PKCE flow:
1. Client initiates OAuth2 authorization code flow with PKCE
2. User authenticates (password, SSO/SAML, or social)
3. Client receives access token + refresh token
4. Scopes are embedded in the JWT claims — no separate scoped token step

Additional enterprise features:
- SAML/SSO support via Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace (using passport-saml library)
- API key rotation without downtime (blue-green key strategy)
- Service account tokens for CI/CD (long-lived, scoped, auditable)

3.3 Migration Plan
- Phase 1 (July): New OAuth2 endpoint live alongside legacy auth
- Phase 2 (August GA): Legacy auth deprecated, 90-day sunset period
- Phase 3 (November): Legacy auth endpoints removed

4. API Gateway Architecture (Connect)

Request flow: Client → CloudFront → ALB → Auth Proxy → Rate Limiter → Router → Target Service

Current p99 latency breakdown:
- Auth proxy: 180ms (bottleneck — doing 3-step token validation on every request)
- Rate limiter: 15ms
- Router: 10ms
- Target service: varies (50-200ms)
- Total p99: ~340ms

Once v3.0 auth ships, the auth proxy simplifies to single JWT validation (~5ms). Expected total p99: <200ms.

5. Data Architecture

PostgreSQL schema highlights:
- users, organizations, teams (multi-tenant)
- api_keys, oauth_clients, sessions (auth)
- integrations, api_endpoints, api_versions (Connect marketplace)
- audit_events (new in v3.0 — currently empty table, will be populated when audit logging ships)
- usage_metrics (per-endpoint call counts, latency, error rates)

All tables use UUID primary keys. Soft deletes where applicable (deleted_at timestamp).

6. Known Technical Debt

1. REST/gRPC dual maintenance: 40% of endpoints still on REST. 3 sprints to complete migration.
2. Auth proxy complexity: Current 3-step validation is the #1 latency bottleneck. Solved by v3.0.
3. Test suite reliability: Integration tests have 15% flaky failure rate. Root cause: shared test database state + async event processing race conditions. Needs dedicated sprint to fix.

Our advantage vs Nexus:
- Deeper integration ecosystem (31 marketplace integrations vs their 8 API testing connectors)
- Better enterprise auth story (once v3.0 ships — right now they're ahead with native SSO)
- Stronger API gateway capabilities — they do testing, not routing/management
- Established customer base with proven use cases

Our risk:
- Their API testing bundling could slow Connect adoption in the SMB segment
- Kira (their new CPO) knows the enterprise playbook from Stripe. They'll get better at enterprise sales.
- If they add API management to their testing suite, the overlap with Connect becomes significant

2. Postman

Still the gorilla in API tooling. 30M+ users, massive brand awareness.
Recent: Launched 'Postman Flows' (API workflow automation). Enterprise pricing aggressive at ~$49/user/month.
Our overlap: Connect's marketplace vs Postman's API platform. They're larger but less focused on the IDE integration angle.
Threat level: HIGH for Connect, LOW for Studio.

Tom frequently references Postman in deal negotiations: 'Meridian's backup plan is Postman.' This is likely true.

3. Kong

Open-source API gateway. Strong in infrastructure layer.
Recent: Kong 4.0 with native gRPC support. Their managed service (Konnect) is growing.
Our overlap: API gateway functionality in Connect. Kong is more mature in pure gateway but doesn't have the marketplace/discovery layer.
Threat level: MEDIUM for Connect gateway, NONE for Studio.

4. JetBrains

Dominant in IDE space (IntelliJ, WebStorm). JetBrains AI assistant improving.
Recent: Fleet (their next-gen IDE) gaining traction. Fleet + AI is their answer to VS Code + Copilot.
Our overlap: Studio competes with their IDEs for developer attention.
Threat level: MEDIUM for Studio (they're focused on traditional IDE, not platform play).

---

Recommendations:
1. Watch Nexus closely — their Series C gives them runway to expand into our space. Kira hire signals enterprise ambitions.
2. Connect's bundling strategy needs a response: can we offer a Studio+Connect bundle at a discount?
3. Auth overhaul (v3.0) is now table-stakes, not a differentiator — Nexus already has SSO. Ship fast.
4. Our moat is the marketplace + gateway combo. Nexus has testing, not management. We should lean into management/governance features that enterprises care about.

[See Figma: link removed — ask Sarah for current Figma access]

- 3 roles × N permissions in a readable format

- Invitation flow that includes role selection

Orion Product Vision: 2026-2027
Author: Anya Patel (CPO) | Presented at: Q3 2026 Kickoff (June 1, 2026)

---

Mission: Make every developer's workflow seamless — from first line of code to production deployment.

Vision (2027): Orion is the default platform for engineering teams that want to build, integrate, and ship without leaving one ecosystem.

We are NOT trying to be:
- A general-purpose IDE (JetBrains, VS Code own this)
- A code hosting platform (GitHub, GitLab own this)
- A pure CI/CD tool (Vercel, Netlify, CircleCI own this)

We ARE trying to be:
- The platform that connects the IDE to the API ecosystem
- The place where engineering teams manage their internal and external API landscape
- The developer-first alternative to enterprise integration platforms (MuleSoft, Apigee)

---

Strategic Pillars

1. Studio: The Developer's Home Base
Studio is our wedge — it's how developers discover Orion. The IDE is good enough to use daily, and the built-in API management tools make it sticky.
- 2026 focus: Enterprise readiness (auth, SSO, RBAC, audit logging)
- 2027 focus: Collaboration (real-time editing, code review, team workspaces)
- Key metric: Daily active developers + NPS

2. Connect: The Growth Engine
Connect is where the money is long-term. API management is a $5B market growing 20% annually. Connect captures this by being the marketplace + gateway that enterprises adopt because their developers already use Studio.
- 2026 focus: Build the marketplace (50 integrations), land 5 enterprise accounts
- 2027 focus: Become the default API gateway for mid-market (replace Kong, Apigee for teams <500 devs)
- Key metric: Integrations published + enterprise ARR

3. Platform Lock-in (Studio + Connect Flywheel)
The magic is the combination. Developers use Studio → discover APIs in Connect → build integrations → publish back to Connect → other developers discover those integrations in Studio.
No competitor offers this full loop. Nexus has an IDE + testing. Postman has testing + docs. Kong has gateway. We have IDE + marketplace + gateway.
- 2026 focus: Seamless Studio↔Connect integration (SSO, shared auth, unified dashboard)
- 2027 focus: Developer analytics across both products (who's using what, team productivity metrics)

---

Growth Strategy

Bottom-up: Free tier → individual developer adoption → team adoption → enterprise expansion
Top-down (new): Enterprise sales motion via Connect (started Q1 2026 with Tom's hire)

Revenue targets:

content:
A/B Test Results: Connect Onboarding Flow v2
Experiment ID: EXP-042
Author: Daniel Park | Date: June 14, 2026
Status: COMPLETE — recommend shipping variant B

---

1. Hypothesis

If we reduce the Connect onboarding from 5 steps to 3 steps (by combining API key creation + first API call into a single guided step, and removing the optional profile completion step), then:
- Activation rate will increase from 45% to 55%
- Time-to-first-API-call will decrease from 45 minutes to 20 minutes
- No negative impact on 30-day retention

2. Test Design

Duration: May 20 — June 10 (21 days)
Traffic split: 50/50 (new Connect signups randomly assigned)
Control (A): Current 5-step onboarding
Variant (B): New 3-step onboarding
Sample size: Control n=203, Variant n=207
Minimum detectable effect: 8% lift at 95% confidence
Tracking: Amplitude (event: connect_onboarding_completed, connect_first_api_call, connect_d30_active)

3. Results

| Metric | Control (A) | Variant (B) | Lift | P-value | Significant? |
|--------|-------------|-------------|------|---------|--------------|
| Activation rate (7-day) | 44.8% | 57.5% | +28.3% | 0.007 | YES |
| Time to first API call | 48 min | 22 min | -54.2% | <0.001 | YES |
| Onboarding completion | 52.2% | 71.0% | +36.0% | 0.001 | YES |
| 30-day retention | 63.1% | 61.8% | -2.1% | 0.42 | NO |
| Support tickets (onboarding) | 18 | 9 | -50.0% | 0.08 | Marginal |

4. Analysis

The 3-step onboarding (variant B) significantly outperformed the current 5-step flow on all primary metrics:

- Activation rate jumped from 44.8% to 57.5%, exceeding our 55% target. The biggest drop-off in the control was between Step 2 (API key creation) and Step 3 (first API call) — 31% abandonment at that boundary. Combining these steps eliminated this friction.

- Time-to-first-API-call cut in half (48min → 22min). The guided "create key + make call" step includes a pre-populated curl command that users can run immediately. No more context switching between docs and the dashboard.

- 30-day retention was statistically unchanged (-2.1%, p=0.42). This was our guardrail metric — we wanted to ensure the faster onboarding didn't create shallow activations that churned quickly. It didn't.

- Support ticket volume dropped 50% (18 → 9), though this is only marginally significant (p=0.08) due to small absolute numbers. Qualitatively, the control's tickets were mostly "how do I make my first API call" and "where do I find my API key" — both addressed by the new guided step.

5. Segment Analysis

| Segment | Control Activation | Variant Activation | Lift |
|---------|-------------------|--------------------|---------|
| Self-serve (no sales touch) | 42.1% | 59.3% | +40.9% |
| Sales-assisted | 51.2% | 53.8% | +5.1% |
| Studio users (cross-product) | 55.0% | 64.7% | +17.6% |
| Non-Studio users | 38.9% | 53.1% | +36.5% |

Key insight: The biggest lift was for self-serve, non-Studio users (+36.5%). These are the users with no prior Orion context — the simplified flow helped them most. Sales-assisted users showed minimal lift, which makes sense — they already had a human guide.

6. Recommendation

Ship variant B to 100% of new Connect signups.

Low-risk decision: primary metric significantly positive, guardrail metric neutral, support load reduced.

Estimated impact at current signup volume (~410/month):
- Additional activations: ~52/month
- Additional conversions (assuming 9.3% conversion rate): ~5/month
- Incremental MRR: ~$1,500/month ($18K/yr)

7. Open Questions / Next Steps

- Should we apply similar simplification to Studio's onboarding? Studio's activation is already at 50% but the OAuth abandonment issue (22% drop-off during auth setup) is worth testing. v3.0 auth changes may fix this organically. Wait until post-v3.0 to decide.
- The removed Step 4 (profile completion) had 0 impact on retention. Can we remove it from Studio too? TBD — need to check if any downstream features depend on profile completeness.

Orion Studio v3.0 — Auth API Specification
Version: 0.9 (DRAFT — subject to change before GA)
Author: Jake Kim | Last updated: June 12, 2026
Format: OpenAPI 3.0 compatible

---

1. Overview

The v3.0 Auth API replaces the legacy 3-step token exchange with a standard OAuth2 + PKCE authorization code flow. This document specifies the new endpoints, request/response schemas, and error handling.

Base URL: https://api.orion.dev/v3/auth
Protocol: HTTPS only (TLS 1.3)
Content-Type: application/json

2. Endpoints

2.1 POST /authorize
Initiates the OAuth2 authorization code flow.

Request:
  client_id: string (required) — Your app's client ID
  redirect_uri: string (required) — Must match registered redirect URI
  response_type: "code" (required)
  scope: string (required) — Space-separated scopes (e.g., "read:api write:api admin")
  state: string (required) — CSRF protection, opaque string
  code_challenge: string (required for PKCE) — Base64url-encoded SHA256 hash of code_verifier
  code_challenge_method: "S256" (required)

Response (302 redirect to redirect_uri):
  code: string — Authorization code (valid 10 minutes, single use)
  state: string — Echoed back for CSRF validation

Errors:
  ERR_INVALID_CLIENT: Client ID not found or disabled
  ERR_INVALID_REDIRECT: Redirect URI doesn't match registered URIs
  ERR_INVALID_SCOPE: One or more requested scopes are invalid
  ERR_PKCE_REQUIRED: PKCE parameters missing (code_challenge, code_challenge_method)

2.2 POST /token
Exchanges authorization code for access + refresh tokens.

Request:
  grant_type: "authorization_code" (required)
  code: string (required) — From /authorize response
  redirect_uri: string (required) — Must match /authorize request
  client_id: string (required)
  code_verifier: string (required for PKCE) — Original code verifier string

Response (200 OK):
  access_token: string — JWT, valid 1 hour
  refresh_token: string — Opaque, valid 30 days
  token_type: "Bearer"
  expires_in: 3600
  scope: string — Granted scopes (may be subset of requested)

Errors:
  ERR_INVALID_GRANT: Code expired, already used, or code_verifier mismatch
  ERR_AUTH_TIMEOUT: Authorization flow took >10 minutes
  ERR_RATE_LIMIT: Too many token requests (max 10/minute per client)

2.3 POST /token (refresh)
Uses refresh token to get a new access token.

Request:
  grant_type: "refresh_token" (required)
  refresh_token: string (required)
  client_id: string (required)

Response: Same as /token (new access_token, same refresh_token unless rotated)

Note: Refresh token rotation is opt-in per client configuration. When enabled, each refresh returns a new refresh_token and invalidates the old one. Meridian requires this (90-day rotation policy).

Errors:
  ERR_REFRESH_EXPIRED: Refresh token has expired (>30 days) or been revoked
  ERR_REFRESH_REUSE: Refresh token was already used (rotation violation — potential token theft, all tokens for this grant are revoked)

2.4 POST /revoke
Revokes an access or refresh token.

Request:
  token: string (required) — The token to revoke
  token_type_hint: "access_token" | "refresh_token" (optional, improves lookup speed)

Response: 200 OK (always — even if token is invalid, to prevent token enumeration)

2.5 GET /userinfo
Returns information about the authenticated user.

Request: Bearer token in Authorization header

Response (200 OK):
  sub: string — User ID (UUID)
  email: string
  name: string
  org_id: string — Organization ID
  roles: string[] — ["admin", "developer", "viewer"]
  scopes: string[] — Scopes granted to the current token

Errors:
  ERR_UNAUTHORIZED: No valid access token provided
  ERR_TOKEN_EXPIRED: Access token has expired (use refresh flow)

3. JWT Claims (Access Token)

{
  "sub": "usr_a1b2c3d4",
  "org": "org_x9y8z7w6",
  "roles": ["developer"],
  "scopes": ["read:api", "write:api"],
  "iss": "https://api.orion.dev",
  "aud": "client_id_here",
  "exp": 1719500400,
  "iat": 1719496800,
  "jti": "tok_unique_id"
}

Signing: RS256 with key rotation every 90 days. JWKS endpoint: GET /v3/auth/.well-known/jwks.json

4. SAML/SSO Integration

For enterprise customers using identity providers (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace):

Endpoint: POST /v3/auth/saml/callback
Supported bindings: HTTP-POST, HTTP-Redirect
NameID formats: emailAddress, persistent
Attribute mapping: configurable per organization via admin dashboard

Setup flow:
1. Customer provides SAML metadata XML (or metadata URL)
2. We configure IdP in org settings (admin-only)
3. Customer adds our SP metadata to their IdP
4. Test with a single user before enabling for org

Known limitation: SAML response must be signed. Unsigned assertions are rejected. Some older IdPs (pre-2020 ADFS) send unsigned assertions — workaround: upgrade IdP or use OAuth2 flow instead.

5. Rate Limits

Endpoint | Limit | Window
/authorize | 30/min per IP | Sliding
/token | 10/min per client | Sliding
/token (refresh) | 20/min per client | Sliding
/revoke | 50/min per client | Sliding
/userinfo | 100/min per token | Sliding

Exceeding rate limits returns HTTP 429 with headers:
  X-RateLimit-Limit: <max requests>
  X-RateLimit-Remaining: <remaining requests>
  X-RateLimit-Reset: <UTC epoch seconds>
  Retry-After: <seconds>

6. Migration from Legacy Auth

Legacy auth (3-step token exchange) will be deprecated August 15 and removed November 15, 2026.

Migration guide: [TBD — Marcos drafting blog post by July 1]
SDK updates: TypeScript SDK v4.0.0, Python SDK v3.0.0, Go SDK v2.0.0 (all in development)
Backward compatibility: Legacy tokens will continue to work during the 90-day sunset period. New token requests via legacy endpoints will return a deprecation warning header.

---

- [ ] Document service account token flow (long-lived tokens for CI/CD)
- [ ] Get security review from pen test firm before GA
- [ ] Finalize SAML attribute mapping defaults

title: Postmortem: API Gateway 502 Outage — June 6, 2026
author: Jake Kim
retrieval_challenge: Incident postmortem with specific timestamps, error codes, and ticket IDs. Tests keyword-heavy retrieval (error codes, ticket IDs, version numbers). Also tests retrieval of root cause analysis.
content:
Postmortem: API Gateway 502 Outage
Date of incident: June 6, 2026, 14:23 — 15:47 UTC (1 hour 24 minutes)
Severity: SEV-1
Author: Jake Kim | Reviewed by: Anya Patel
Status: Action items in progress
Incident ticket: INC-2026-0047

---

1. Summary

On June 6, 2026, the Orion Connect API gateway experienced intermittent 502 Bad Gateway errors affecting approximately 340 enterprise API consumers for 84 minutes. Root cause: a connection pool exhaustion bug triggered by a surge in webhook delivery retries from a single large customer (Atlas Corp). The issue was not caught by monitoring because our 502 alert threshold was set too high (>5% error rate, actual peak was 4.7%).

2. Impact

- Duration: 84 minutes (14:23 — 15:47 UTC)
- Users affected: ~340 API consumers across 8 enterprise accounts + ~1,200 free/pro tier users
- Error rate: peaked at 4.7% of all API requests (normal: <0.1%)
- Failed API calls: ~12,400 (estimated from gateway access logs)
- Revenue impact: None directly, but Atlas Corp opened escalation ticket CONNECT-743 and threatened contract termination if not resolved by June 30
- SLA impact: 3 enterprise customers dropped below 99.95% monthly SLA threshold for June

3. Timeline (all times UTC)

14:23 — Atlas Corp's webhook processor begins retry loop for 847 failed webhook deliveries from their deployment pipeline. Each retry spawns a new connection to the API gateway.

14:31 — Gateway connection pool (max 500 connections) reaches 480 connections. No alert — connection pool monitoring was set up in Datadog but the alert was disabled during a maintenance window in May and never re-enabled. JIRA: CONNECT-891 (missed re-enable).

14:38 — Connection pool exhausted at 500/500. New connections start timing out. Gateway returns 502 for ~2% of requests. First customer support ticket received (BluePeak Software, ticket: SUP-2026-4421).

14:42 — PagerDuty fires alert: "Connect API error rate above 2%" (lower threshold alert). On-call engineer (Taylor) acknowledges.

14:45 — Taylor identifies 502s in the gateway access logs. Initial hypothesis: upstream service failure. Checks Studio backend — healthy. Checks Connect backend — healthy. Connection pool not checked because the Datadog dashboard didn't surface it (dashboard widget was filtered to exclude connection metrics — UI bug in the dashboard config).

14:58 — Error rate spikes to 4.7%. Second PagerDuty escalation. Jake paged.

15:02 — Jake joins incident channel. Checks raw ECS metrics directly (bypassing Datadog dashboard). Identifies connection pool at 500/500 with 200+ connections from a single source IP. Cross-references with API key: Atlas Corp.

15:08 — Jake identifies Atlas Corp's webhook retry loop as the trigger. Each failed webhook spawns a new HTTP connection with a 30-second timeout. With 847 retries and 30s timeouts, they're holding ~100 connections at any given time.

15:12 — Mitigation: Jake increases connection pool max from 500 to 1000 via ECS task definition update. Deployment takes ~8 minutes.

15:20 — New task definition deployed. Connection pool expands. Error rate drops to 1.2%.

15:35 — Atlas Corp's retry queue drains. Connection count normalizes. Error rate returns to <0.1%.

15:47 — Incident declared resolved. Monitoring confirmed stable for 12 minutes.

4. Root Cause

Primary: The API gateway's connection pool (500 max) does not implement per-client connection limits. A single customer (Atlas Corp) consumed ~100 concurrent connections (20% of the pool) during a webhook retry storm, leaving insufficient connections for other customers.

Contributing factors:
1. Connection pool monitoring alert was disabled during May maintenance and never re-enabled (CONNECT-891)
2. Datadog dashboard was misconfigured to exclude connection pool metrics (UI-level filter, not a data issue)
3. Webhook retry logic uses exponential backoff but doesn't cap total concurrent connections per client
4. Gateway connection pool max (500) was set 18 months ago when traffic was 5x lower — never revisited

5. Action Items

| # | Action | Owner | Ticket | Due | Status |
|---|--------|-------|--------|-----|--------|
| 1 | Implement per-client connection limits in gateway | Sam | CONNECT-892 | Jun 20 | In progress |
| 2 | Re-enable connection pool alert in Datadog | Taylor | CONNECT-891 | Jun 7 | DONE |
| 3 | Fix Datadog dashboard filter to include connection metrics | Taylor | CONNECT-893 | Jun 10 | DONE |
| 4 | Add connection pool utilization to standard monitoring runbook | Pat | CONNECT-894 | Jun 14 | DONE |
| 5 | Increase default connection pool to 1000 (permanent) | Jake | STUDIO-1847 | Jun 13 | DONE |
| 6 | Add per-client connection cap to webhook retry logic | Riley | CONNECT-895 | Jun 25 | In progress |
| 7 | Audit all alert thresholds — ensure no disabled alerts from maintenance windows | Taylor | CONNECT-896 | Jun 30 | Not started |
| 8 | Post-incident communication to affected enterprise customers | Maya | CS-RISK-097 | Jun 8 | DONE |

6. Lessons Learned

- Connection pool sizing should be reviewed quarterly as traffic grows. We hadn't touched it in 18 months.
- Disabled alerts during maintenance windows are a landmine. We need a process to re-enable after maintenance completes. Proposal: auto-expire maintenance windows after 48 hours.
- Our monitoring dashboards had a silent configuration error that hid relevant metrics. Dashboards need periodic audits too — not just the alerts.
- Single-tenant connection abuse is a known pattern in multi-tenant systems. We should have had per-client limits from day one. This is the same class of issue Meridian flagged with rate limiting.

7. Detection Gap

Why didn't we catch this faster?
- Connection pool alert: disabled (root cause)
- 502 error rate alert: threshold set at 5%, peak was 4.7% — we were UNDER the alert threshold. Action: lower to 2% (already done as part of incident response).
- Customer-reported: the first signal was a support ticket (14:38), 15 minutes after impact started. We should be detecting before customers do.

Estimated MTTR without the detection gap: ~30 minutes instead of 84. We lost 54 minutes to detection failure.

---

Follow-up review: June 20 (all action items due by then or explicitly deferred)

Last revised: April 15, 2026

1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "Personal Data" means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person, as defined by applicable Data Protection Laws.

1.2 "Processing" means any operation performed on Personal Data, including collection, storage, modification, retrieval, use, disclosure, and erasure.

1.3 "Data Protection Laws" means the General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679 ("GDPR"), the California Consumer Privacy Act ("CCPA"), and any other applicable data protection legislation.

1.4 "Sub-processor" means any third party engaged by Processor to Process Personal Data on behalf of Controller.

1.5 "Security Incident" means any unauthorized access to, or acquisition, use, modification, disclosure, or destruction of, Personal Data.

2. SCOPE OF PROCESSING

2.1 Processor shall Process Personal Data solely for the purpose of providing the Orion platform services as described in the Master Service Agreement ("MSA") between the parties.

2.2 Categories of Personal Data Processed:
  (a) Developer account information (name, email, organization)
  (b) API usage data (endpoints called, request metadata, timestamps)
  (c) Authentication credentials (hashed passwords, OAuth tokens — encrypted at rest)
  (d) Product usage analytics (feature usage, session data — anonymized where possible)

2.3 Categories of Data Subjects:
  (a) Employees and contractors of Controller who use the Orion platform
  (b) End users of Controller's applications that integrate with Orion APIs

3. PROCESSOR OBLIGATIONS

3.1 Processor shall:
  (a) Process Personal Data only on documented instructions from Controller
  (b) Ensure that persons authorized to Process Personal Data have committed to confidentiality
  (c) Implement appropriate technical and organizational security measures (see Section 5)
  (d) Assist Controller in responding to Data Subject requests (access, deletion, portability)
  (e) Delete or return all Personal Data upon termination of the MSA, at Controller's choice
  (f) Make available to Controller all information necessary to demonstrate compliance

3.2 Processor shall not engage any Sub-processor without prior written consent of Controller. Controller hereby consents to the Sub-processors listed in Annex B.

4.1 Personal Data is stored and Processed within the United States (AWS us-east-1 region).

4.2 For transfers of Personal Data from the European Economic Area (EEA) to the United States, the parties shall rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (Module 2: Controller to Processor) as set forth in Annex C.

4.3 Processor shall notify Controller before making any changes to the data Processing location.

5. SECURITY MEASURES

5.1 Processor implements the following technical measures:
  (a) Encryption at rest: AES-256 for all databases and storage (AWS RDS encryption, S3 server-side encryption)
  (b) Encryption in transit: TLS 1.3 enforced for all connections

Note: Sections marked [PENDING] reflect measures in active development. Processor commits to implementing all pending measures by Q4 2026.

6.1 Processor shall notify Controller of any Security Incident without undue delay and in any event within 72 hours of becoming aware of such incident.

Change Management Plan: API Auth Migration (Studio v3.0)
Author: Jake Kim | Reviewed by: Anya Patel, Marcos Rivera
Last updated: June 14, 2026
Status: APPROVED — execution begins July 1

---

1. Overview

This plan covers the migration from Orion's legacy 3-step token exchange auth to the new OAuth2 + PKCE flow. The migration affects all Studio and Connect API consumers.

Scope:
- ~3,200 active API consumers (2,100 Studio, 1,100 Connect)
- 12 enterprise accounts with production integrations
- 19 partner-built Connect integrations
- Internal services: 8 microservices using service-to-service auth

Timeline:
- Phase 1 (July 1-14): New auth endpoints deployed alongside legacy
- Phase 2 (Aug 15 — GA): Legacy auth deprecated, new auth is default
- Phase 3 (Nov 15): Legacy auth endpoints removed

2. Feature Flags

We're using LaunchDarkly for the auth migration. Flags:

Flag: auth-v3-enabled
Description: Enables new OAuth2 endpoints in production
Default: false
Rollout plan: 5% → 25% → 50% → 100% (over 2 weeks)

Flag: auth-legacy-deprecated
Description: Returns deprecation warning header on legacy auth requests
Default: false
Enable date: August 15 (GA)

Flag: auth-legacy-blocked
Description: Blocks legacy auth requests entirely (returns 410 Gone)
Default: false
Enable date: November 15

Flag: auth-saml-enabled
Description: Enables SAML/SSO endpoints for enterprise customers
Default: false
Rollout: Per-organization flag (manually enabled per customer request)

Each flag can be instantly toggled. Rollback = disable auth-v3-enabled + disable auth-legacy-deprecated. All traffic routes back to legacy within ~30 seconds (CDN cache TTL).

3. Rollback Procedures

Level 1 (Minor issues — individual customers affected):
- Symptom: <1% of auth requests failing on new flow
- Action: Route affected customers back to legacy via LaunchDarkly targeting rules
- Owner: On-call engineer
- Recovery time: <5 minutes
- Escalation: Not required unless >5 customers affected

Level 2 (Major issues — widespread failures):
- Symptom: >5% auth failure rate on new flow, OR any enterprise customer reporting issues
- Action: Disable auth-v3-enabled flag globally. All traffic routes to legacy.
- Owner: On-call engineer + Jake (paged)
- Recovery time: <2 minutes (flag toggle) + ~30 seconds (CDN propagation)
- Escalation: Anya notified, incident channel opened

Level 3 (Critical — data integrity or security issue):
- Symptom: Token leakage, unauthorized access, or data corruption
- Action: Disable auth-v3-enabled + revoke ALL v3 tokens + force re-authentication
- Owner: Jake (directly) + security response
- Recovery time: <10 minutes for flag + token revocation. Customer re-auth may take hours.
- Escalation: Leo, Anya, Tom notified. Customer communication within 1 hour.
- Post-incident: Full postmortem required within 48 hours

4. Risk Matrix

Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation
SDK incompatibility (customer's SDK version too old for PKCE) | HIGH | MEDIUM | Provide SDK upgrade guide + migration script. Legacy fallback available.
Enterprise SAML configuration errors | MEDIUM | HIGH | Pre-test with each enterprise customer before enabling. Dedicated support channel.
Token format change breaks customer middleware | MEDIUM | MEDIUM | New JWT format documented 30 days before GA. Provide JWT validation library.
gRPC services fail to recognize new tokens | LOW | HIGH | Internal service migration completed before external rollout.
Connection pool issues under new auth load | LOW | MEDIUM | Load tested at 3x current peak. Connection pool sized at 1000 (post-outage fix).
Customer confusion about deprecation timeline | HIGH | LOW | Blog post, email campaign, in-app banner, documentation updates. 90-day sunset period.

5. Communication Plan

T-30 days (July 15):
- Blog post: "Introducing Orion's new authentication experience" (Marcos authoring)
- Email to all API consumers: migration timeline, what's changing, link to migration guide
- In-app banner: "New auth coming August 15 — see migration guide"

T-14 days (August 1):
- Email #2: Reminder + specific action items for each auth method
- Enterprise customers: 1:1 call with CSM to review migration steps
- Partner program: Dedicated Slack channel for migration support

T-0 (August 15 — GA):
- Legacy deprecation header enabled
- Blog post update: "New auth is live"
- Documentation updated: new auth flow is primary, legacy marked deprecated

T+90 days (November 15 — Sunset):
- Email #3: Final warning, legacy endpoints going away
- Legacy auth blocked (410 Gone responses)

6. Testing Plan

Before Phase 1 (July 1):
[✅] Unit tests: 100% coverage on new auth endpoints (142 tests)
[✅] Integration tests: OAuth2 flow, PKCE validation, token refresh, token revocation
[✅] Load test: 3x current peak (15K req/min) — passed, p99 < 50ms
[🔄] Pen test: Scheduled for week of June 23 with CyberSafe LLC. Results expected June 30.
[❌] Enterprise customer pre-test: Scheduled with Meridian (June 28), Crestline (June 30), BluePeak (July 2)

Before Phase 2 (August 15):
[❌] 2-week soak period at 100% rollout on new auth with legacy fallback available
[❌] All 12 enterprise customers successfully migrated to new auth
[❌] All 19 partner integrations tested with new auth
[❌] SDK updates published (TypeScript v4.0, Python v3.0, Go v2.0)

7. Dependencies

| Dependency | Owner | Status | Risk |
|------------|-------|--------|------|
| gRPC migration at 80% | Jake | 60% complete | MEDIUM — must hit 80% before auth ships |
| SDK updates published | Sam + Riley | Not started | LOW — 2 weeks work, starting July 1 |
| Pen test results clean | External (CyberSafe) | Scheduled Jun 23 | MEDIUM — critical findings could delay GA |
| Meridian pre-test successful | Maya + Priya | Scheduled Jun 28 | HIGH — Meridian is THE customer for this feature |
| Blog post published | Marcos | Draft by July 1 | LOW |
| LaunchDarkly flags configured | Pat | Done | — |

Q2 2026 Retrospective — Product Team
Author: Anya Patel | Date: May 30, 2026

What we shipped in Q2:

1. Studio v2.5 GA (shipped February, but Q2 included the stabilization and adoption push)
   - Plugin marketplace reached 23 community plugins (up from 12 at launch)
   - Dark mode adoption: 67% of users enabled it within 2 weeks
   - Editor performance: load time stable at 1.8s (down from 3.2s in v2.4)

2. Connect marketplace growth
   - Integrations: 15 → 31 (doubled!)
   - First external partner (DataForge) through self-serve onboarding
   - API gateway shipped (basic routing + rate limiting)

3. Team restructuring (March)
   - Created dedicated Studio and Connect squads
   - Hired Priya Sharma as Connect PM
   - Moved 2 engineers from cancelled Mobile pilot to Connect

4. Mobile pilot + kill decision
   - Ran 8-week pilot (April-May)
   - Results were clear: low adoption, high cost
   - Killed June 2. Right call, should have been faster.

What we didn't ship:

1. Collaboration features — pushed AGAIN. Third time.
2. SOC2 preparation — didn't start. Still no owner.
3. Advanced search — cut from v2.5, not yet rescheduled
4. Connect self-serve billing — Stripe integration still manual for Enterprise

Q2 metrics recap:
- ARR: $2.8M → $4.2M (50% growth)
- Customers: 105 → 140
- NPS: 48 → 52
- Churn: 4.8% → 4.2%

Grade: B+. Revenue and growth are ahead of plan. Product execution was good on the things we shipped. But we keep accumulating strategic debt (collaboration, SOC2, search) that will catch up to us.

Q2 lessons:
1. Kill decisions should be faster. We knew at week 4 of the Mobile pilot that it wasn't working. We waited until week 8.
2. The reorg worked. Having dedicated squads for Studio and Connect was the single best organizational decision of the quarter.
3. Enterprise requirements (auth, SOC2, audit logging) are accumulating faster than we're shipping them. Q3 is enterprise-or-bust.
4. Priya was a great hire. She's already owning the Meridian relationship and the partner program. Good instinct by the hiring committee.
